text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A conference on money laundering, sponsored by the U.N. Drug Control Programme (UNDCP), opened in Riga. The three Baltic prime ministers signed a joint declaration saying they would step up efforts to fight against money laundering.
- Parliament confirmed two more judges for the Constitutional Court which means it be able to start work.

- The district Court of in the western region of Kurzeme sentenced to death Vladimir Lisik for carrying out a triple murder and heavy bodily injuries. It is the first death sentence passed this year although President Guntis Ulmanis earlier suspended capital punishment.

- The LNNK party, part of the government coalition, and the small People's Christian Party issued a statement saying that Latvia's position in talks with Russia must be based on the 1920 peace treaty and the declaration on Latvia's occupation, passed by parliament this year. They also criticised Latvia's current foreign policy on Russia.

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele met the vice-president of Scandinavian Airlines Lars Lindgren to discuss the chances of Air Baltic, in which SAS has a large stake, fyling to Russia. Shkele said he was ready to solve the problem, employing political and economical means.
- Parliament has granted Latvian citizenship for special merits to four hockey-players of the national team as well as a surgeon in a rural hospital.
- President Guntis Ulmanis continues his visit to the UK.

- Five deputies elected from the list of the Latvian Socialist Party, two of them supported by the left-oriented movement For Equal Rights (Lidztiesiba), agreed to form a parliamentary faction The Socialist Party Lidztiesiba.
- Parliament voted to set up a committee to investigate the activities of the Latvian Radio and TV council which they accuse of incompetence and acting in its members own interests.

- The EBRD has affirmed its interest in financing some projects in Latvia such as the construction of a pulp mill, modernisation of railways and Riga international airport. EBRD officials said financing the modernisation of the railway could start in 1998 and cost between $50 million and $60 million.
